links.outcome: Whether complex agentic architectures outperform a simple single agent for code status extraction
links.effect: For capable models (GPT-OSS-20B, MedGemma-27B-IT, Qwen3.5-27B), single agents matched or beat complex systems; multiagent review doubled tokens and latency without accuracy gains. Reflection impaired MedGemma DNI (P=.047).
links.quote: For capable larger models (GPT-OSS-20B, MedGemma-27B-IT, Qwen3.5-27B), single-agent architectures achieved comparable or superior performance for explicit code status (DNR, DNI) relative to complex systems, whereas multiagent review doubled token consumption and latency without accuracy gains.

links.outcome: Accuracy, token use and latency of complex agentic architectures versus simpler single-agent baseline on same data
links.effect: Architectural complexity did not improve extraction in capable LLMs. Multiagent review helped only the 8B model (DNR P=.017, CMO P<.001), still below clinically acceptable performance.
links.quote: Architectural complexity does not enhance extraction performance for capable LLMs, and reflective self-review may cause conservative overcorrection.

unlisted_practices: Matching agentic architecture complexity (self-reflection, extractor-reviewer) to task characteristics and model capability rather than adopting by default

screen.reason: The study directly tests agentic verification safeguards (single agent with self-reflection and multiagent extractor-reviewer pipelines) against standard single-agent generation across multiple LLMs for clinical code status extraction.

primary.practice: reflective self-review and multiagent extractor-reviewer architecture
